From: Oliver Chen <oliver@datasync.io>

Subject: Unexpected invoice spikes - Sept ingest overage?

Hi Stephanie,

We pulled the September invoice and theres a big jump compared with our July/Aug numbers: total token usage attributed to our ingest pipeline is ~42% higher. I attached the PDF of the invoice (invoice_sept.pdf) — line items look like raw usage by API key.

Can you do two things for us:
- Confirm which API keys / project IDs were billed for the large bulk uploads on 2026-09-14 and 2026-09-21.
- Provide a CSV export showing per-request attribution (request_id, api_key, timestamp, token_count) for Sept 1-30.

We run an async ingest job that sometimes retries on error; could the retries be double-counted? Were in Ireland and also need to ensure VAT has been applied correctly (reverse-charge or not) on the corrected invoice.

Were paused on payments for the disputed portion pending evidence — accounts-payable@datasync.io is copied.

Thanks,
Oliver
Director of Platform
Datasync Ltd.

Attachments: invoice_sept.pdf (pdf, 128KB)

Subject: Re: Unexpected invoice spikes - Sept ingest overage? — preliminary findings

Hi Oliver / team,

Thanks for the patience — pulled the token traces for your account and attached the raw export (usage_export_202609.csv) plus a sampled ingest trace (ingest_trace_617.jsonl). Preliminary observations:

1) We see a cluster of requests on 2026-09-14 and 2026-09-21 where the same upstream job generated identical payloads but with distinct request_ids due to our SDKs retry wrapper on failed ACKs. The retries were scheduled ~1.2s apart and each generated token billing. That aligns with your hypothesis about retries being double-counted.

2) There is an async re-ingest from your pipeline on 2026-09-21 at 03:02:17Z where the ingestion coordinator re-submitted a batch that had already succeeded. The re-submission created a new set of request_ids; Redwoods metering attributes per-request_id, so both submissions were billed.

Root cause: duplicate submissions at the client side combined with .
Metering behavior: current attribution is per-request_id; there is no automatic de-duplication across request payload hashes.

Proposed remediation:
- We will issue a manual credit for duplicated token usage. Based on the traced samples, estimated duplicated tokens = 2,350,412 tokens (approx. $3,420 at your plan rates).
- We can re-issue a corrected invoice and a credit memo (credit_memo_draft.pdf) and mark the resulting adjustment as EU reverse-charge neutral (we will confirm VAT classification with finance).
- Engineering recommendation: we can add a lightweight de-dupe heuristic for async ingest pipelines (optionally opt-in) to detect identical payload hashes within a short window; we can scope that as a small feature request (timeline ~2-3 weeks for pilot).

Please confirm youd like us to proceed with the credit and the corrected invoice, and whether you want the raw traces posted to the HubSpot-linked Drive (we will lock access to your account only).

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Billing Manager, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

Attachments: usage_export_202609.csv (csv, 1.2MB), ingest_trace_617.jsonl (jsonl, 420KB)

If that works, Ill schedule a call for Tue or Wed this week and attach a credit memo draft for sign-off. Once you confirm the credit, well suspend the disputed hold for AP and route the corrected invoice to your billing mailbox.
